title: Six agents at once, at most three gates at once
what: relay's own kit.toml sets max_parallel = 6 (the routing hook's cap follows it). `relay gate` takes one of N machine-wide slots before it starts its steps (N = 3, set in the machine's ~/.relay config or an env var for tests), waits for a free slot printing one line, and frees it on exit, crash or kill (a lock that a dead process cannot hold). The default for other projects stays 4 agents (front's decision, owner can reverse). After the next wave, compare merged changes per hour with the wave before.
why: Owner, 26 Oct: "Является ли лимит одновременно запущенных агентов бутылочным горлышком ? Стоит ли его увеличить" then "a" (6 agents, gates capped at 3). Measured on 238 gates (12 cores): library tests median 138 s alone, 280-350 s with 1-3 others, 489 s with 4+; gates per hour peak near 4 at once and fall at 5+. Gates are 40-60% of a change's time; build, review and check wait on the model. Expected +25-30% (an estimate to check). IP chosen by the front (agent-chosen).
where: .claude/kit.toml [delegate] max_parallel, bin/relay gate (lib: the gate runner), rules/delegation.md ("At most 4 agents at once unless the project says otherwise")
